newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government plans to announce measures on pharmaceutical pricing policy today, aiming at culling 100 billion drachmas annually. The cutbacks will hit producers and marketers - domestically-produced medicines however will be supported by special price lists while imported medicines will have their prices set on the basis of the lowest price in European Union countries.

--Albania's election campaign moves to downtown Athens today when Albanian socialist leader Fatos Nano addresses a rally of his compatriots resident in Athens. Nano received assurances of support for free and fair elections and to allow immigrants unhindered passage to Albania to vote from Prime Minister Costas Simitis and Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos yesterday.
--Greenpeace and Development Minister Vasso Papandreou yesterday celebrated the government's investment in the largest solar power plant in the world on Crete yesterday.
--An inquiry is under way at the Greek Police into the drafting of lists of senior police officials and their alleged political and other allegiances.

--The tax department is using the carrot before the stick in its attempts to recoup the 1.6 trillion drachmas owed it from around 1,000 taxpayers. A letter will be sent to all debtors asking them to settle their debts.
--Education ministry employees took to the roads yesterday to demand the payment of their bonuses: their actions continue to put the fate of general examinations this month in doubt.
--The mayor of Ilioupolis, a suburb of Athens, has forwarded to the public prosecutor false certificates of incapacity to work signed by local doctors and used by workers for "sickies".

--Violence in the south of Albania, thought to be directed from the ruling party in Tirana, to undermine general elections later this month, has forced the Albanian opposition to ask for Athens support to deal with the problem.
--Technical problems led to chaos at Athens airport yesterday and things are expected to be worse today as thousands of Athenians head off on the long weekend.

--The Schengen Treaty and its provisions to abolish check on internal borders will threaten the status of Mount Athos, the autonomous monastic community, the monks say. The monks have sent an urgent letter to Athens demanding a reiteration of the ban on women.
--Former prime minister Constantine Mitsotakis reveals his thoughts on the appointment of Rhicard Holbrooke as US presidential emissary on Cyprus.
--The government is promoting its plans for a three-year "truce" in labour relations with an agreement to regulate wages and schedules. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
